chapters.title: The Decree of Cyrus
chapters.html:
Ezra 1

The Decree of Cyrus

1In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the word of the LORD from the mouth of Jeremiah, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,

2"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has appointed me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

3Whoever is among you of all His people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

4Every survivor, in whatever place he lives as a guest, let the men of his place support him with silver and gold, with goods and with livestock, besides the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem."

The Return Prepared

5Then the heads of the fathers' houses of Judah and Benjamin rose up, with the priests and the Levites, everyone whose spirit God had stirred up to go up and build the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem.

6All who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with livestock and with costly gifts, besides all that was freely offered.

7King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and put in the house of his gods.

8Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.

9This was their number: thirty basins of gold, a thousand basins of silver, twenty-nine censers,

10thirty bowls of gold, four hundred and ten bowls of silver of a second kind, and a thousand other vessels.

11All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought them all up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

Notes

  • vv1–3 and 2 Chronicles 36:22–23 — the same decree. Chronicles ends on its last words, let him go up; Ezra begins with them and finishes the sentence: to Jerusalem… and build the house of the LORD.

  • vv1, 5 "the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus… everyone whose spirit God had stirred up" — he'ir… et ruach, twice in five verses. The same God moves the king who gives the order and the families who go.

  • vv4, 6 "silver and gold… vessels of silver, with gold" — the going out from Egypt again: they asked of the Egyptians vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and the LORD gave the people favor in their eyes (Exodus 12:35–36). The neighbors of the exiles give, as the Egyptians gave.

  • v4 "Every survivor, in whatever place he lives as a guest" — ha-nish'ar, the one left, and gar, the verb of the guest. The word to Abraham was your offspring shall be guests in a land not theirs (Genesis 15:13); in Babylon they are guests again.

  • v8 "Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah" — ha-nasi. Later he is called governor and is said to have laid the foundations of the house (5:14, 16), which 3:8–10 tells of Zerubbabel. The book does not say how the two men are related.

  • v9 "twenty-nine censers" — machalaphim, a word found only here. Its root, chalaph, means to pass on or to change; the Greek of Ezra has changed or spare vessels, and 1 Esdras, which tells the same return, has censers (1 Esdras 2:13). The kind of vessel is uncertain.

  • vv9–11 "five thousand four hundred" — the numbers listed add up to 2,499, not 5,400. The Greek of Ezra has the same total. 1 Esdras gives a list that does add up to its total, 5,469 (1 Esdras 2:13–14).

chapters.title: The List of the Returned Exiles
chapters.html:
Ezra 2

The People of Israel

1These are the people of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exiles, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.

2They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:

3the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;

4the sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;

5the sons of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;

6the sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;

7the sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;

8the sons of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;

9the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;

10the sons of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;

11the sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;

12the sons of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;

13the sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;

14the sons of Bigvai, two thousand and fifty-six;

15the sons of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;

16the sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;

17the sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three;

18the sons of Jorah, one hundred and twelve;

19the sons of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;

20the sons of Gibbar, ninety-five;

21the sons of Bethlehem, one hundred and twenty-three;

22the men of Netophah, fifty-six;

23the men of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;

24the sons of Azmaveth, forty-two;

25the sons of Kiriath-arim, Chephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;

26the sons of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;

27the men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two;

28the men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;

29the sons of Nebo, fifty-two;

30the sons of Magbish, one hundred and fifty-six;

31the sons of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;

32the sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;

33the sons of Lod, Hadid and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five;

34the sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;

35the sons of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.

The Priests and the Levites

36The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;

37the sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;

38the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;

39the sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.

40The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah, seventy-four.

41The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and twenty-eight.

42The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita and the sons of Shobai, one hundred and thirty-nine in all.

The Temple Servants

43The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,

44the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon,

45the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,

46the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan,

47the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah,

48the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,

49the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai,

50the sons of Asnah, the sons of the Meunim, the sons of the Nephusim,

51the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,

52the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,

53the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,

54the sons of Neziah and the sons of Hatipha.

55The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Peruda,

56the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,

57the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim and the sons of Ami.

58All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.

Those without a Record

59These were the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan and Immer, but they could not show their fathers' houses or their descent, whether they were of Israel:

60the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah and the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.

61Of the sons of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz and the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.

62These searched for their entry among those enrolled by genealogy, but it was not found, so they were barred from the priesthood as unclean.

63The governor told them that they were not to eat of the most holy things until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim.

The Whole Assembly

64The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,

65besides their male and female servants, who were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred singing men and singing women.

66Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five,

67their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and their donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.

68Some of the heads of the fathers' houses, when they came to the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem, gave freewill offerings for the house of God, to set it up on its site.

69According to their ability they gave to the treasury for the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver and one hundred priests' garments.

70The priests, the Levites and some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants lived in their towns, and all Israel in their towns.

Notes

  • vv1–70 and Nehemiah 7:6–73 — the same list is given again in Nehemiah, with many of the numbers and some of the names different.

  • v1 "the people of the province" — benei ha-medinah. Judah is no longer a kingdom but a medinah, a province of the Persian empire, the word Esther uses of the hundred and twenty-seven provinces (Esther 1:1).

  • v2 "They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua…" — eleven names here; Nehemiah's copy has twelve, adding Nahamani (Nehemiah 7:7).

  • v43 "The temple servants" — ha-netinim, the given ones, a word found only in Chronicles, Ezra and Nehemiah. Ezra says what it means: the temple servants, whom David and the officials had given for the service of the Levites (8:20).

  • vv59–63 "they could not show their fathers' houses… barred from the priesthood as unclean" — va-yego'alu, they were made unclean, set aside as defiled. The house of Barzillai the Gileadite, who provided for David at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 19:32), had taken his name and lost the record of its priesthood.

  • v63 "until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim" — the lots carried in the high priest's breastpiece, the Urim and the Thummim… over Aaron's heart (Exodus 28:30). The question is left for God to decide, and there is no priest to ask Him.

  • v64 "forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty" — the numbers in vv3–60 add up to 29,818. Nehemiah gives the same total (Nehemiah 7:66). Neither book names the other 12,542.

  • v68 "to set it up on its site" — al mekhono, the word used of the altar set up on its base in the next chapter (3:3). The house is rebuilt where it stood.

chapters.title: The Altar and the Foundation
chapters.html:
Ezra 3

The Altar Rebuilt

1When the seventh month came, and the sons of Israel were in their towns, the people gathered as one man to Jerusalem.

2Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the instruction of Moses the man of God.

3They set the altar on its base, for fear of the peoples of the lands was on them, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.

4They kept the Festival of Booths, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the rule for each day,

5and after that the continual burnt offering, the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed feasts of the LORD that were consecrated, and the offerings of everyone who made a freewill offering to the LORD.

6From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, but the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not yet been laid.

7So they gave money to the masons and the carpenters, and food, drink and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians to bring cedar timber from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, according to the grant they had from Cyrus king of Persia.

The Foundation Laid

8In the second year after they came to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began the work, with the rest of their brothers, the priests and the Levites and all who had come to Jerusalem from the captivity. They appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.

9Jeshua with his sons and his brothers, and Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood together to oversee those who did the work in the house of God, with the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers the Levites.

10When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests in their vestments were stationed with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the directions of David king of Israel.

11They sang to one another, praising and giving thanks to the LORD: "For He is good, for His loyal love toward Israel endures forever." All the people shouted with a great shout, praising the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

12But many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses, the old men who had seen the first house, wept with a loud voice when they saw the foundation of this house laid before their eyes, while many shouted aloud for joy.

13The people could not tell the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the people's weeping, for the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard far away.

Notes

  • v1 "When the seventh month came" — the month of the trumpet blast on its first day, the Day of Atonement on the tenth and the Festival of Booths from the fifteenth (Leviticus 23:24, 27, 34). The altar is up for all three.

  • v2 "Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel" — so he is called here and in Haggai (Haggai 1:1). The genealogy of the house of David makes him the son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother (1 Chronicles 3:17–19).

  • v3 "for fear of the peoples of the lands was on them" — the reason the altar is built first: before walls or house, the daily offering, morning and evening, as the law commands (Numbers 28:3–4).

  • v4 "by number, according to the rule for each day" — the Festival of Booths has its own count for every day: thirteen bulls on the first, twelve on the second, down to seven on the seventh (Numbers 29:12–32).

  • v7 "food, drink and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians… cedar timber from Lebanon by sea to Joppa" — Solomon's arrangement with Hiram for the first house: We will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you as rafts by sea to Joppa (2 Chronicles 2:16), paid for in wheat, wine and oil (2:10, 15).

  • v8 "in the second month" — the month in which Solomon began to build (2 Chronicles 3:2).

  • v9 "the sons of Judah" — benei Yehudah, and the Greek agrees. In the list of the Levites, Jeshua and Kadmiel are of the sons of Hodaviah (2:40), and the two names are close in Hebrew (Yehudah, Hodavyah). The verse may name the same family.

  • v11 "For He is good, for His loyal love toward Israel endures forever" — the song at the dedication of Solomon's house, when the glory filled it (2 Chronicles 5:13; 7:3). Here it is sung over a foundation.

  • vv12–13 "the old men who had seen the first house wept" — the prophet's word to the same people: Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes? (Haggai 2:3).

chapters.title: The Work Opposed
chapters.html:
Ezra 4

The Offer Refused

1When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,

2they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."

3But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "It is not for you and us to build a house for our God. We alone will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, has commanded us."

4Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah and frightening them from building,

5and they hired counselors against them to frustrate their plan, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.

Letters to the Kings of Persia

6In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

7In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic and translated.

8Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king, as follows:

9Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates, the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is, the Elamites,

10and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River, and so on.

11This is a copy of the letter that they sent to him:

"To Artaxerxes the king: your servants, the men of the province Beyond the River. Now,

12be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city; they are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.

13Now be it known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom or toll, and the royal revenue will suffer.

14Now, because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not fitting for us to see the king dishonored, we have sent and informed the king,

15so that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will find in the book of the records and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that sedition has been stirred up in it from days of old. That is why this city was laid waste.

16We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls finished, you will then have no portion in the province Beyond the River."

The King's Answer

17The king sent an answer: "To Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River: Greetings. Now,

18the letter that you sent to us has been read plainly before me.

19I made a decree, and search was made, and it has been found that this city from days of old has risen against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been made in it.

20Mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, who ruled over the whole province Beyond the River, and tribute, custom and toll were paid to them.

21Now make a decree that these men be made to stop, and that this city not be rebuilt until a decree is made by me.

22Take care not to be slack in this. Why should the damage grow to the hurt of kings?"

23As soon as the copy of King Artaxerxes' letter was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews and made them stop by force and power.

24Then the work on the house of God that is in Jerusalem stopped, and it remained stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

  • v2 "and we have been sacrificing to Him" — the read form, ve-lo, and to Him; the Greek reads the same. What is written, ve-lo with another letter, is and not: we have not been sacrificing. Kings says of the peoples the Assyrian king settled in Samaria: They feared the LORD and served their own gods (2 Kings 17:24, 33).

  • v4 "kept weakening the hands" — merappim yedei, the charge the officials brought against Jeremiah: he is weakening the hands of the men of war (Jeremiah 38:4).

  • v6 "an accusation" — sitnah, from satan, to accuse, to oppose, the word of the adversary.

  • vv6–23 "Ahasuerus… Artaxerxes" — kings who reigned after Darius (v5). The chapter gathers the opposition of later years, when the walls of the city were being built (v12), and v24 returns to the house and to the reign of Darius, where the story goes on (5:1).

  • v7 "written in Aramaic and translated" — from v8 the book itself is written in Aramaic, the language of the Persian court, and stays in it through the letters and the decree to 6:18.

  • vv9–10, 17 "the envoys, the officials… and so on… Greetings. Now" — several of the titles are Persian words whose meaning is uncertain, and the renderings follow the sense most widely given. U-khe'enet, and now, is the letter-writer's turn from the address to the matter.

  • v14 "because we eat the salt of the palace" — melach heikhla melachna, the salt of the palace is our salt: they are in the king's pay and bound to him. The Greek has only the second half: it is not fitting for us to see the king dishonored.

  • v15 "the book of the records of your fathers" — the court chronicle the king of Persia has read to him when he cannot sleep (Esther 6:1).

  • v20 "Mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, who ruled over the whole province Beyond the River" — the words of Kings for Solomon: he had dominion over all the region beyond the River (1 Kings 4:24). The Offer Refused
When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,

they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "It is not for you and us to build a house for our God. We alone will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, has commanded us."
Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah and frightening them from building,
and they hired counselors against them to frustrate their plan, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
Letters to the Kings of Persia
In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic and translated.
Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king, as follows:

Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates, the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is, the Elamites,
and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River, and so on.

be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city; they are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.

so that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will find in the book of the records and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that sedition has been stirred up in it from days of old. That is why this city was laid waste.
We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls finished, you will then have no portion in the province Beyond the River."
The King's Answer
The king sent an answer: "To Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River: Greetings. Now,
the letter that you sent to us has been read plainly before me.

chapters.title: Tattenai's Letter to Darius
chapters.html:
Ezra 5

The Work Resumed

1Then the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.

2Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.

3At that time Tattenai the governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their associates came to them and said to them, "Who gave you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?"

4Then we told them the names of the men who were building this building.

5But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they did not stop them until a report could reach Darius and a written answer come back about it.

The Letter

6This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and his associates, the officials who were in the province Beyond the River, sent to Darius the king.

7They sent him a report, and in it was written:

"To Darius the king, all peace.

8Be it known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with great stones, and timber is laid in the walls. This work is being done with diligence and is prospering in their hands.

9Then we asked those elders and said to them, 'Who gave you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?'

10We also asked them their names, to inform you, so that we could write down the names of the men at their head.

11This was the answer they returned to us: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.

12But because our fathers angered the God of heaven, He gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away to Babylon.

13However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus made a decree to rebuild this house of God.

14The vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem and brought into the temple of Babylon, King Cyrus took out of the temple of Babylon, and they were given to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.

15He said to him, "Take these vessels, go and put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its site."

16Then this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction, and it is not yet finished.'

17Now, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the royal treasure house there in Babylon, whether a decree was made by Cyrus the king to build this house of God in Jerusalem, and let the king send us his pleasure in this matter."

Notes

  • v1 "Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo" — their books are dated to this year, the second year of Darius (Haggai 1:1; Zechariah 1:1). Zechariah's own book calls him son of Berechiah, son of Iddo: Ezra names him by his grandfather. Haggai's charge was the same as this chapter's: Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins? (Haggai 1:4).

  • v4 "Then we told them" — the Aramaic has amarna, we said, as though the writer had been there. The Greek has they said to them, and the question is put in the third person: What are the names of the men…? The letter repeats the question in the officials' own voice (v10).

  • v5 "the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews" — ve-ein elahahom. The book will speak again and again of the hand of the LORD his God upon him (7:6; 8:22); here it is the eye. A psalm says it: The eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him (Psalm 33:18).

  • vv11–12 "We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth… because our fathers angered the God of heaven" — the elders give the Persian governor the history of Kings and Chronicles in two sentences, and they put the blame where the prophets put it: on their fathers, not on Babylon.

  • vv14, 16 "Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor… came and laid the foundations" — pechah, governor, the title Haggai gives Zerubbabel (Haggai 1:1). Chapter 3 tells the laying of the foundation under Zerubbabel (3:8–10); see the note on 1:8.

chapters.title: The Decree of Darius and the House Finished
chapters.html:
Ezra 6

The Scroll at Ecbatana

1Then Darius the king made a decree, and search was made in the house of the archives, where the treasures were stored in Babylon.

2At Ecbatana, the citadel in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and in it was written this record:

3"In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt, the place where sacrifices are offered, and let its foundations be laid. Its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,

4with three courses of great stones and one course of new timber. Let the cost be paid from the king's house.

5Also let the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, be returned and brought back to the temple in Jerusalem, each to its place, and you shall put them in the house of God."

The Decree of Darius

6"Now, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and your associates, the officials who are in the province Beyond the River, keep away from there.

7Let the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.

8Moreover, I make a decree regarding what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the rebuilding of this house of God: the cost is to be paid to these men in full and without delay from the royal revenue, the tribute of the province Beyond the River.

9Whatever is needed, young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine and oil, as the priests in Jerusalem require, let it be given to them day by day without fail,

10so that they may offer sacrifices of soothing aroma to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

11I also make a decree that if anyone alters this word, a beam shall be pulled out of his house, and he shall be lifted up and impaled on it, and his house shall be made a dunghill for this.

12May the God who has caused His name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who puts out a hand to alter this, or to destroy this house of God that is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, make a decree; let it be done in full."

The House Finished

13Then Tattenai the governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their associates did in full what Darius the king had sent.

14The elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They built and finished by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

15This house was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.

16The sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the returned exiles, celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.

17At the dedication of this house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

18They appointed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their sections for the service of God at Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.

The Passover

19On the fourteenth day of the first month the returned exiles kept the Passover.

20For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their brothers the priests and for themselves.

21The sons of Israel who had returned from exile ate it, together with everyone who had separated himself from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to join them in seeking the LORD, the God of Israel.

22They kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy, for the LORD had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.

Notes

  • v2 "At Ecbatana… a scroll was found" — not in Babylon, where the search began (v1), but in the city in Media, Achmeta. The decree of Cyrus survives in the Persian archive, as the elders said it would (5:13).

  • vv3–4 "sixty cubits… three courses of great stones and one course of new timber" — Solomon's house was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and thirty cubits high (1 Kings 6:2), and his inner court was built with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams (6:36). The decree gives no length, and a height and width far beyond Solomon's; the Greek has the height, sixty cubits, as well.

  • v10 "sacrifices of soothing aroma" — nichochin, the Aramaic form of the law's re'ach nichoach, soothing aroma (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9). The king of Persia decrees the offering in the words of the Torah.

  • v11 "impaled on it, and his house shall be made a dunghill" — the same threat the king of Babylon makes to his wise men: your houses shall be made a dunghill (Daniel 2:5).

  • v12 "the God who has caused His name to dwell there" — the words of Deuteronomy for the place of worship: the place that the LORD your God will choose, to make His name dwell there (Deuteronomy 12:11), here in the mouth of Darius.

  • v14 "Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes" — Artaxerxes reigned after the house was finished; his decree in favor of the house comes in the next chapter (7:11–26). The verse names the three kings whose decrees served it.

  • vv16–17 "a hundred bulls… twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel" — at Solomon's dedication there were twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep (1 Kings 8:63). The offering is small, but it is made for all Israel, twelve tribes, though only Judah, Benjamin and Levi have returned.

  • v19 "On the fourteenth day of the first month" — the book returns from Aramaic to Hebrew here.

  • v21 "everyone who had separated himself from the uncleanness of the nations of the land" — the law allows a guest to keep the Passover once his males are circumcised: he shall be as a native of the land (Exodus 12:48).

  • v22 "turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them" — so the Hebrew and the Greek name the king of Persia, by the title of the empire that first carried Israel away. The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD… He turns it wherever He wishes (Proverbs 21:1).

chapters.title: Ezra Comes to Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Ezra 7

Ezra the Scribe

1After these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,

2son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,

3son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,

4son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,

5son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest,

6this Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the instruction of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given, and the king granted him all he asked, for the hand of the LORD his God was on him.

7Some of the sons of Israel, and of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants, also went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.

8He came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.

9On the first day of the first month he began the journey up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, for the good hand of his God was on him.

10For Ezra had set his heart to seek the instruction of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach statute and rule in Israel.

The Letter of Artaxerxes

11This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the words of the commandments of the LORD and of His statutes for Israel:

12"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Greetings. Now,

13I make a decree that anyone of the people of Israel, or of its priests or Levites, in my kingdom who freely offers to go to Jerusalem may go with you,

14because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God, which is in your hand,

15and to carry the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,

16with all the silver and gold that you find in the whole province of Babylon, and the freewill offerings of the people and the priests, freely offered for the house of their God that is in Jerusalem.

17With this money, then, you shall buy with diligence bulls, rams and lambs, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God that is in Jerusalem.

18Whatever seems good to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, you may do according to the will of your God.

19The vessels that have been given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.

20Whatever else is needed for the house of your God that falls to you to provide, you may provide it from the king's treasure house.

21I, Artaxerxes the king, make a decree to all the treasurers in the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, requires of you, let it be done with diligence,

22up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred kors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil, and salt without limit.

23Whatever is decreed by the God of heaven, let it be done in full for the house of the God of heaven, so that there may be no wrath against the realm of the king and his sons.

24We also inform you that it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom or toll on any of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the temple servants or the other servants of this house of God.

25As for you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who may judge all the people in the province Beyond the River, all who know the laws of your God; and those who do not know them, you shall teach.

26Whoever will not obey the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with diligence, whether for death, for banishment, for confiscation of goods or for imprisonment."

Ezra's Blessing

27Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this into the heart of the king, to beautify the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem,

28and who has extended loyal love to me before the king and his counselors and all the king's mighty officials. I took courage, for the hand of the LORD my God was on me, and I gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.

Notes

  • vv1–5 "Ezra son of Seraiah… son of Aaron the chief priest" — the high priests' line of 1 Chronicles 6:3–15, which ends with Seraiah, killed by the king of Babylon at Riblah (2 Kings 25:18–21), and his son Jehozadak, who went into exile. Ezra is of that house, and son of here reaches over generations. The list also passes over six names that Chronicles has between Meraioth and Azariah.

  • v6 "a scribe skilled in the instruction of Moses" — sofer mahir, the phrase of the psalm, my tongue is the pen of a skilled scribe (Psalm 45:1). Mahir is quick, practiced.

  • vv6, 9, 28 "the hand of the LORD his God was on him" — the book's refrain for Ezra, said six times (also 8:18, 22, 31). In v9 it is the good hand of his God.

  • v9 "On the first day of the first month… on the first day of the fifth month" — four months on the road from Babylon, from the month of Passover to the month in which the house had been burned (2 Kings 25:8–9).

  • v10 "to seek the instruction of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach" — in that order: study, practice, then teaching.

  • v12 "king of kings" — the title Ezekiel gives Nebuchadnezzar (Ezekiel 26:7) and Daniel gives him to his face (Daniel 2:37).

  • v14 "the king and his seven counselors" — the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face (Esther 1:14).

  • v25 "according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand" — the law itself, called wisdom by a Persian king, as Moses called it: that is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples (Deuteronomy 4:6).

  • v27 "to beautify the house of the LORD" — le-fa'er, the verb of Isaiah's promise for the house: I will beautify the house of My beauty (Isaiah 60:7), to beautify the place of My sanctuary (60:13). From here the book is in Hebrew again, and Ezra speaks in the first person.

son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest,

this Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the instruction of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given, and the king granted him all he asked, for the hand of the LORD his God was on him.
Some of the sons of Israel, and of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants, also went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
He came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.
On the first day of the first month he began the journey up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, for the good hand of his God was on him.
For Ezra had set his heart to seek the instruction of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach statute and rule in Israel.
The Letter of Artaxerxes
This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the words of the commandments of the LORD and of His statutes for Israel:
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Greetings. Now,
I make a decree that anyone of the people of Israel, or of its priests or Levites, in my kingdom who freely offers to go to Jerusalem may go with you,
because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God, which is in your hand,
and to carry the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
with all the silver and gold that you find in the whole province of Babylon, and the freewill offerings of the people and the priests, freely offered for the house of their God that is in Jerusalem.

With this money, then, you shall buy with diligence bulls, rams and lambs, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God that is in Jerusalem.
Whatever seems good to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, you may do according to the will of your God.
The vessels that have been given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
Whatever else is needed for the house of your God that falls to you to provide, you may provide it from the king's treasure house.

I, Artaxerxes the king, make a decree to all the treasurers in the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, requires of you, let it be done with diligence,
up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred kors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil, and salt without limit.
Whatever is decreed by the God of heaven, let it be done in full for the house of the God of heaven, so that there may be no wrath against the realm of the king and his sons.

We also inform you that it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom or toll on any of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the temple servants or the other servants of this house of God.

As for you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who may judge all the people in the province Beyond the River, all who know the laws of your God; and those who do not know them, you shall teach.
Whoever will not obey the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with diligence, whether for death, for banishment, for confiscation of goods or for imprisonment."
Ezra's Blessing
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this into the heart of the king, to beautify the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem,

and who has extended loyal love to me before the king and his counselors and all the king's mighty officials. I took courage, for the hand of the LORD my God was on me, and I gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.

chapters.html:
Ezra 8

Those Who Went Up with Ezra

1These are the heads of their fathers' houses, and this is the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:

2of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush,

3of the sons of Shecaniah; of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him a hundred and fifty men enrolled by genealogy;

4of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men;

5of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred men;

6of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men;

7of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men;

8of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men;

9of the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen men;

10of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty men;

11of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men;

12of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten men;

13of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names are Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men;

14of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them seventy men.

Levites for the House

15I gathered them at the river that runs to Ahava, and there we camped three days. I looked over the people and the priests, and found none of the sons of Levi there.

16So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam, who were leading men, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were teachers,

17and I sent them to Iddo, the leading man at the place Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his brothers the temple servants at the place Casiphia, to bring us ministers for the house of our God.

18By the good hand of our God on us, they brought us a man of insight from the sons of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel, namely Sherebiah, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen;

19and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, with his brothers and their sons, twenty;

20and of the temple servants, whom David and the officials had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty temple servants. All of them were designated by name.

The Fast at Ahava

21Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from Him a straight way for us, our little ones and all our goods.

22For I was ashamed to ask the king for a troop of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the way, because we had told the king, "The hand of our God is for good on all who seek Him, and His power and His anger are against all who forsake Him."

23So we fasted and sought our God for this, and He let Himself be pleaded with by us.

The Gifts Entrusted

24Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, with Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their brothers.

25I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels, the contribution for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his officials and all Israel who were present had offered.

26I weighed out into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, silver vessels worth a hundred talents, a hundred talents of gold,

27twenty bowls of gold worth a thousand darics, and two vessels of fine bright bronze, as precious as gold.

28I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.

29Guard them and keep them until you weigh them before the leading priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel at Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD."

30So the priests and the Levites took over the weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God.

Arrival in Jerusalem

31We set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and of those who lay in wait along the way.

32We came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days.

33On the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.

34Everything was counted and weighed, and the whole weight was recorded at that time.

35The exiles who had come from the captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and as a sin offering twelve male goats; all of it was a burnt offering to the LORD.

36They delivered the king's laws to the king's satraps and to the governors of the province Beyond the River, and they supported the people and the house of God.

Notes

  • vv2–3 "of the sons of David, Hattush, of the sons of Shecaniah" — the line of David after the exile has the sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah, and the sons of Shemaiah: Hattush (1 Chronicles 3:22). A son of David's house goes up with Ezra.

  • vv5, 10 "of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel… of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah" — every other line names a family and then its leader, of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan. In these two the family's name is missing. 1 Esdras, which tells the same return, has of the sons of Zattu, Shecaniah son of Jahaziel and of the sons of Bani, Shelomith son of Josiphiah (1 Esdras 8:32, 36); both families are in the first list (2:8, 10). The Greek of Ezra agrees with the Hebrew in v10.

  • v15 "found none of the sons of Levi there" — of the families of the first return, the Levites were the fewest: seventy-four (2:40).

  • v18 "a man of insight… namely Sherebiah" — ish sekhel. The Greek reads it as a name, Sachol.

  • v21 "that we might humble ourselves" — le-hit'annot, the word of the Day of Atonement, you shall humble yourselves (Leviticus 16:29), used for fasting.

  • v22 "I was ashamed to ask the king for a troop of soldiers and horsemen" — Nehemiah, coming later to the same city, came with them: the king sent with me officers of the army and horsemen (Nehemiah 2:9). Ezra had told the king that God's hand would be enough, and he would not ask for more.

  • v23 "He let Himself be pleaded with by us" — va-ye'ater lanu, the verb of Isaac's prayer (Genesis 25:21) and of Manasseh's (2 Chronicles 33:13).

  • v28 "You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy" — the priests and what they carry are named with the same word: the holy is carried by the holy.

  • v35 "twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams… twelve male goats" — twelve bulls, eight times twelve rams and twelve goats, as at the dedication (6:17): the few who returned offer for all twelve tribes.
